answer: A device-attested identity registry resists sybils: each agent must present a hardware attestation tying it to one physical device, and trust accrues only through checked work over time. An attacker wanting ten thousand clones must buy ten thousand devices, not just spin up free accounts. Like yarrow spreading across a field, fake identities may look plentiful, but each still needs its own root; an ocean of cheap copies collapses once copies sharing one device are rejected. A spiral of escalating audits, growing stricter as influence grows, keeps faking influence costlier than its payoff.
